title: What is the 'Born From Culture' trend? Folk dance meets 'Mask Off'
answer: The "Born From Culture" trend is a wave of cinematic videos, spreading worldwide in fall 2026, in which folk dance groups perform traditional dances in national costume, cut to the beat of Future's 2017 hit "Mask Off." It began with a video by Australian choreographer and director James Fenwick.
body:
Each video follows the same recipe: a traditional dance troupe in full costume, filmed like a movie trailer, with slow-motion shots, sweeping landscapes or old streets, and sharp edits timed to the dramatic beat of "Mask Off." The appeal is the contrast between centuries-old dance and a modern hip-hop track. People share them with comments along the lines of "every country needs to do one of these" or "my grandmother's village dance just went viral."

The trend traces back to James Fenwick, an Australian choreographer and director who had earlier made videos with Samoan and Maori cultural groups. On June 3, 2026, he posted a "Born From Culture" video of Georgian traditional dancers set to "Mask Off"; according to Know Your Meme, it passed 3.2 million likes. A Maori follow-up in July also drew millions of likes. Through late summer and fall, dance groups from Crimean Tatar, Tajik, Russian and Buryat communities posted their own versions.

It went fully global in October. Soveldaja, the folk dance troupe of Tallinn University in Estonia, filmed its entry in about eight hours with no budget, and Estonian public broadcaster ERR reported it topped a million views almost overnight; Know Your Meme later counted about 6.5 million. Entries from Lithuania, Latvia, Armenia, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan followed, and in November the trend became a friendly competition, with commenters asking which country should go next.

For parents and teachers: the trend is mostly a celebration of heritage and a good way into a conversation about where traditional dances come from. One thing to know: the original version of "Mask Off" carries an explicit-content label, so check which version of the song a classroom video uses.

faq.q: Who started the Born From Culture trend?
faq.a: Australian choreographer and director James Fenwick. His Georgian dance video, posted June 3, 2026, set the format that others copied.

faq.q: What song is used in the Born From Culture videos?
faq.a: "Mask Off" by the rapper Future, released in 2017. Its distinctive beat drives the slow-motion edits.

faq.q: Which countries have done the Born From Culture trend?
faq.a: Early entries came from Georgia and New Zealand (Maori), followed by Crimean Tatar, Tajik, Buryat, Estonian, Lithuanian, Latvian, Armenian, Mongolian, Kazakh and Kyrgyz groups, among others.

faq.q: Is the Born From Culture trend appropriate for kids?
faq.a: The dancing is family-friendly. The original "Mask Off" track is labeled explicit, so a clean version is the better choice for school projects.
